name: Anuj Kapoor

thesis.text: I go where technology is rewriting economics and markets,

strap: Right now that means making a forest as legible to markets as a bond, threading solar energy systems with a distributed platform, putting Himalayan supply chains on digital rails, and building digital intelligence that lets a small team move at the scale of an institution. Trained as a digital economist, banker and product builder, wired as a founder, and drawn into policy and strategy to help design the rules that best guide future systems, I spend half my time contemplating emerging technologies and the other half helping build them.
workNote: Open to partnerships built on shared value.

tile.title: About me
tile.teaser: Having built products and ventures across domains for over twenty years, I have honed a system for adapting quickly to emerging innovations, to create value and help solve real-world problems. I believe it is crucial to keep an adaptive working model of the world that stays current even as technology changes exponentially.

panel.title: How human systems and economics change when technology arrives

blocks.text: One question has run through my career: how do people and their economics evolve when new technology arrives?

I built a wide, multidisciplinary educational base, reading economics, Renaissance literature, philosophy and business. Realising on graduating that ICTs and software would be among the most defining elements of our time, I went to the London School of Economics for an MSc to study how new media and information systems, at the dawn of social media, were shaping the evolution of social and economic systems. Understanding how technology reshapes economies also meant understanding how capital moves. I spent the next eight years inside its machinery, first at Citigroup's EMEA Treasury in Canary Wharf, then setting up a structured investments desk at EFG Private Bank in Mayfair.

By 2011–12 a new field was emerging: decentralised systems and distributed economics, driven by Satoshi Nakamoto's 2008 paper. Here was an information system redesigning money, trust and institutions. I left banking in 2012 to follow it and see it work in the real world.

From peer-to-peer economic systems and decentralised communication platforms to the semantic web and digital intelligence (from 2018), I look to spot each evolutionary step in technology early, learn its economic and social impact in depth, then put it to work where it can make a difference: in a Himalayan village, in a gamified augmented-reality world, in natural assets, in renewable energy infrastructure, inside an AI system and in policy.
Deeply multidisciplinary: I enjoy going deep enough into a new field to build something that really works, then connecting it to everything else I know.

items.text: Data, data intelligence and fintech for environmental markets. Built Green Intelligence, an AI project-data environment that maps renewable, nature-based carbon and environmental projects against markets, regulations and registries.

items.title: Five Benches · Founder Director
items.text: Supply chains for provenance-rich goods from the lower Himalayas, built with villages and women's self-help groups: production systems, digital identity, e-commerce, logistics and direct sales in London and Europe.

subs.title: Himalayan chilli farmers
subs.text: Through Himalayan People I gave [Chamba Chukh](https://himalayanpeople.com/collections/himachillichukh), a chilli preserve made by a remote community of chilli growers and women's self-help groups, its [digital identity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamba_chukh), and built its supply chain from the villages to [export and e-commerce](https://himalayanpeople.com/pages/chukh-recipes-snacking-and-cooking-ideas) markets.

subs.title: A digital brand for Himalayan weavers
subs.text: Woolaah: handcrafted products made by master weavers working with rural Himalayan women's self-help groups, in pure wool and silk, dyed by hand with eco-friendly dyes.

items.title: Trading digital assets and working on distributed systems
items.text: Trading and experimenting with Bitcoin and other digital assets while researching distributed systems: white papers on data harvesting, intelligence and consensus for proof-of-truth systems, and DLT use cases in finance, supply chains and data validation.

items.title: EFG Private Bank, Mayfair · Advisory
items.text: Set up the advisory cross-asset structured products desk, working on buy-side packaged products and derivatives for the bank's portfolio managers and private banking clients. Responsible for the bank's investment-banking relationships, I managed credit and counterparty risk, successfully navigating the bank's portfolios through the credit crisis.

items.title: Citigroup EMEA Treasury, London · Resident Vice President
items.text: Structured and traded cross-asset derivatives and structured notes (fixed income, equity, credit, commodities and alternatives) for Citigroup's EMEA businesses, as part of EMEA Treasury at Canary Wharf, London.

I have been fortunate to be in the rooms where those discussions happen, helping make sure the new road is built for both speed and safety.

items.text: Vers l'Azur!, a mixed-media concert at the Royal Academy of Music, London. I created a visual installation to accompany a classical pianist performing Claude Debussy's Preludes: a first-of-its-kind symbolic rendition of a piano recital in mixed media.

items.title: Village to market stalls
items.text: Helping weavers move from craft to repeatable production, then flying to London to run market stalls in Hampstead, Marylebone, Spitalfields, Chelsea and beyond, pitching the product and selling it face to face.

items.title: Chamba Chukh, from a remote valley to the world map
items.text: Working with chilli growers and women's self-help groups in a remote Himalayan community, I created the digital identity for their community product, Chamba Chukh, and launched it on the web. I built the whole supply chain from the villages to export and e-commerce markets, putting it on the global map of provenance-rich chilli products. It drew attention from national news channels and media, and the state government later put it forward for Geographical Indication (GI) certification.

items.title: A London short film at the LA Short Film Festival
items.text: I wrote and produced The Fate of Choice, a short film shot around London with students from the London Film School. It was featured at the Los Angeles Short Film Festival and screened at a theatre in West London.

panel.title: From the hills of Shimla to London

blocks.text: Born and raised in Shimla, a small Himalayan hill station in north India, into a family of doctors, engineers and lawyers. Educated in cities around the world, I now live in London and work on projects in both India and the UK, and in several countries in Africa.

items.text: Published writer and poet, former market researcher and creative director. Co-founder of Five Benches, helping Himalayan makers create market-ready products.

items.label: Partner
items.title: Digital transformation
items.text: Leadership roles in digital transformation, including Global Head of Digital Strategy and Head of Product, and software consulting for world-leading organisations. Dog lover and passionate supporter of animal welfare programmes.

blocks.text: Several of my creative ventures began by solving small problems for the people around me. Himalayan People started as a way to connect communities near where I was born to digital markets. Festive People is a game I designed so my family could celebrate festivals together from wherever we were. Green Intelligence came from noticing that hardworking small enterprises and makers in rural communities struggled to pitch their work to funders and grant makers. It now does that for them, leaving them free to get on with their real work, which is in atoms, not digits.
